headline: Automated workflows map raw microbial sequencing and AST data to trait and safety calls
label: Microbial Genomics Analysis Pipelines
summary: Recent preprints and publications package genomic and phenotypic microbial analyses as user-accessible, containerized web tools.
synthesis: The common thread is the automation of microbial analysis as end-to-end workflows that take raw input through to interpretive calls on traits or safety. BGX, a Dockerized and scalable pipeline, chains genome retrieval, quality checks, AMR profiling, and biosynthetic gene cluster novelty and bioactivity prediction. RATION-GUI provides a public web workflow for whole genome shotgun hazard analysis of bacterial and fungal biocontrol agents, covering QC, taxonomy, AMR, and pathogenicity. J-AST differs in input modality, operating on disk diffusion and Epsilometer susceptibility data rather than genomes, but follows the same workflow logic as an open-source web platform. EzMAP v2.0 and ClusterApp apply similar integrated packaging to amplicon microbiome and LC-MS/MS metabolomics data, respectively, outside the genomic scope of the other items. What is new is the packaging of these analyses as end-to-end, user-accessible tools rather than the underlying methods themselves.
